subtopic: Planning a trip on a budget
subtype: Approach: buffer for delays and extra costs [Thinking]
passage: Come here, Reena, you're planning your school trip, so sit and hear Siddharth Dada's story. When I was seventeen, we went by train to Kolkata with 2,000 rupees each. My father said, “Keep ten percent aside and don't touch it.” So I held back 200 rupees in a tin at the bottom of my bag. And in every day's plan I left one empty hour. On the second day the train came three hours late. My friends panicked. I just slid the museum into my empty hour, and we saw everything. On the third day tea and snacks at the station cost double what we had expected, and my 200 covered the difference. The boys who had planned every minute and every rupee spent the last day borrowing and rushing. A little slack is not waste, beta.

qa.q: How much did Siddharth hold back?
qa.a: Siddharth held back 200 rupees in a tin at the bottom of my bag.

qa.q: What did Siddharth's friends feel when the train came three hours late?
qa.a: They panicked, since their tight plans had no room for a delay.

qa.q: Which choice worked in the story, and why?
qa.a: Sliding the museum into the empty hour worked, because the spare hour absorbed the delay without ruining the day.

qa.q: How might the boys who planned every minute have felt at the end of the trip?
qa.a: They were probably stressed and hurried, since they spent the last day borrowing money and rushing.

grounding: A teen adds a ten percent reserve and one spare hour each day, so a late train or a price rise does not ruin the schedule.

passage: Yash's plan for the Darjeeling trip looked almost boring. Tenzin, reading it over his shoulder at the station, pointed at one line: "Spare: 450 (10% of 4,500)." "Why keep money doing nothing?" "Because something always goes wrong," Yash said. "And every day has one empty hour. See, after lunch." Tenzin shrugged. Then the announcement came: their train from Siliguri was running ninety minutes late. Rain had slowed everything on the line. Tenzin groaned. Yash was already recounting. "We lose today's empty hour, plus a bit. So we skip the tea shop and still reach the homestay before dark." In Darjeeling, the shared jeep to the monastery cost more than the website had said. Yash paid the difference from the spare. By day three, the plan had bent twice and nothing had broken.

qa.q: How late was the train from Siliguri?
qa.a: The train from Siliguri was running ninety minutes late.

qa.q: What does Yash's quick recounting suggest about how he felt when the delay was announced?
qa.a: Yash stayed calm rather than panicked, because the spare hour meant a delay was a problem he had already expected.

qa.q: What else could Yash try if a delay ran much longer than the spare hour?
qa.a: He could decide in advance which stop is first to drop each day, so a big delay means one quick cut instead of a scramble.

qa.q: How might Tenzin see the boring spare line by day three?
qa.a: Tenzin, who shrugged it off at first, likely sees its worth after the delay and the costlier jeep, since the empty hour and the spare money kept the trip on track.

grounding: Shows a teen keeping a ten percent money reserve and a spare hour each day, so a late train and a higher jeep fare do not wreck the plan.

passage: "Just fill every hour, na," Tushar said, scrolling the list of Mumbai sights on Ramesh's laptop in the colony reading room. Ramesh shook his head. "Last year our class missed the aquarium because the bus got stuck in traffic for an hour. Everything after that fell like dominoes." He typed a line into each day: "Free hour, 3 to 4." Then under money: "2,000 each, keep 200 aside." "Ten percent for what?" "Prices change. Or someone's slipper breaks. If we don't need it, we eat something nice on the last night." On Saturday, the ferry to Elephanta cost forty rupees more each than the price they had found online. Tushar paid it from the kept-aside money without a word, then grinned at Ramesh. "Fine. Your boring hour can stay too."

qa.q: How much did Ramesh plan to keep aside out of 2,000 each?
Why did Ramesh insist on a free hour each day?
qa.a: Ramesh was still wary after last year, when one hour stuck in traffic made everything after it fall like dominoes.

qa.q: What else could help if a delay and a price rise hit on the same day?
qa.a: They could choose in advance one sight to drop first, so the free hour and the spare money cover the rest without an argument on the spot.

qa.q: How does Tushar see the buffer by Saturday?
qa.a: Tushar first wanted every hour filled, but after the ferry cost more, Tushar grins and accepts both the spare money and the free hour.

grounding: Illustrates a teen reasoning aloud for a ten percent reserve and a spare hour daily, which later absorbs a rise in the ferry price.
